endorsements.quote: This can be furthered with so-called model cards, which are short documentations of the context, usage, and evaluation in varied conditions (e.g., across different populations).

Describing the analysis pipeline, from data preprocessing to cluster description and post-hoc analyses, as well as recording/providing logs of re-runs, provide a high-level understanding of the model used, and therethrough explainability .

unlisted_practices: Assess stability of ML-derived clusters by resampling the data and measuring cluster-wise and participant-wise stability when external validation data are unavailable.
Involve clinical domain experts throughout the ML clustering pipeline and foster close collaboration between clinicians and methodologists.
Use multiple relevant internal validation metrics rather than a single measure, combined with clinical evaluation, when selecting the number of clusters.
Assess the clinical relevance of ML-derived subgroups by testing association with clinically relevant outcomes such as treatment response, disease events, or death.
Ensure ML-derived subgroups can be identified by clinicians using simple, feasible sets of variables, and report measures of certainty in cluster label assignment.
Clearly describe the purpose of a cluster analysis study and select an appropriate study sample for the clinical context.
Externally validate ML-derived clusters in an independent population to confirm subgroup robustness.

screen.reason: The paper proposes a methodological framework and guidelines for evaluating the clinical utility, stability, and generalizability of ML-derived disease clusters.
